_validation_note: The 14-day window (June 1–15, 2026) yielded three candidates with in-window news triggers. Zero passed all seven gates. The window was broadened to 21 days (May 25–June 15) per protocol. Zero passed all seven gates in the 21-day window either. Dominant failure mode: Gate 5 (chokepoint asymmetry). Mechanisms with valid news ties and verifiable layer chains (GCI cable break, GVEA pricing) both have multi-actor or physical/environmental chokepoints rather than a single named institutional officer with a binary decision. The RCA is a 5-member commission; the repair vessel constraint is environmental. Second failure mode: Gate 1 paraphrase drift — AO 2026-27's trigger article (June 9 RFLP story) does not name the mechanism it purports to trigger. Gate 1 requires the trigger article to make the mechanism visible. The APFC IPS trigger is an institutional self-announcement, not independent editorial coverage. No candidate passes all seven gates after applying both windows. This is a correct no-target outcome. The bar was not lowered. Recommendation for next cycle: surface mechanisms with single administrative law judge decisions, single contracting officer award decisions, or single-signature permit approvals — these will be more likely to pass Gate 5 than rate cases, board votes, or market-driven physical constraints.
